scenarios.name: single, small private IRA withdrawal well under both the $6,000 cap and the income threshold: clean pass
scenarios.source: Form MO-A (2025), page 3, 'Part 3 - Pension and Social Security/Social Security Disability', 'Private Pension Calculation - Annuities, pensions, IRAs, and 401(k) plans funded by a private source.' Section B worksheet: Line 1 Missouri AGI, Line 2 taxable Social Security, Line 3 = Line1-Line2, Line 4 threshold ($25,000 single/head of household/qualifying widow(er), $32,000 married filing combined, $16,000 married filing separate), Line 5 = Line3-Line4 (floor $0), Line 6 taxable private pension/IRA/401(k) income, Line 7 = lesser of Line 6 or $6,000, Line 9 = Line 7 minus Line 5 (floor $0). Single filer, IRA withdrawal $5,000, no other income: Line3 = 5000-0 = 5000, well under the $25,000 threshold so Line5 = $0 (Line4 > Line3). Line7 = min(5000,6000) = 5000. Line9 = 5000-0 = 5000, i.e. the full $5,000 withdrawal is excluded. Missouri AGI = 5000-5000 = 0. Missouri conforms to the federal standard deduction (RSMo 143.131); 2026 single standard deduction is $16,100, which alone exceeds the $5,000 of income, so taxable income is $0 either before or after the exclusion. Tax = $0.

scenarios.name: single, larger private IRA withdrawal: the $6,000 cap is fully phased out above the $25,000 income threshold
scenarios.source: Same Form MO-A Section B as above. Single filer, IRA withdrawal $50,000, no other income. Line3 = 50000-0 = 50000. Line4 (single threshold) = 25000. Line5 = 50000-25000 = 25000 (reduction). Line7 = min(50000,6000) = 6000 (the raw pre-reduction cap). Line9 = 6000-25000, Line5 exceeds Line8, per the form's own instruction ('If Line 5 is greater than Line 8, enter $0') the exclusion is $0. Missouri AGI = 50000 (fully taxable). Standard deduction (single, age 60, no 65+ addback) = $16,100. Missouri taxable income = 50000-16100 = 33900. Missouri's 2026 brackets (dor.mo.gov 2025 MO-1040 Instructions page 21 chart, escalated by the same year-over-year CPI adjustment MO applies annually -- 2026 thresholds of $1,348/$2,696/$4,044/$5,392/$6,740/$8,088/$9,436 at 2%/2.5%/3%/3.5%/4%/4.5%/4.7% are corroborated against the 2025 chart's $1,313/.../$9,191 progression and independently by multiple 2026-specific bracket calculators). Cumulative tax through the $9,436 top-bracket floor = 262.86 (sum of each $1,348-wide band's tax). Tax = 262.86 + 0.047*(33900-9436) = 262.86+1149.81 = $1,412.67.

knownDefect.summary: RetireSmartIRA/Resources/StateTaxData/2026/statetax-2026-MO.json's config sets iraWithdrawalExemption to .full (unconditional), but Form MO-A Section B caps private pension/IRA/401(k) income at $6,000 per taxpayer, phased out dollar-for-dollar above $25,000 single / $32,000 MFJ Missouri AGI. This is not the public-pension cap the 2026-08-02 audit already flagged; it is a separate, unaudited gap that is directly on-point for this app's core IRA-withdrawal/Roth-conversion use case, and is expressible with the existing .partial(maxExempt:) + AGIPhaseout(.linear(perDollar: 1.0)) machinery already used elsewhere in this codebase.

scenarios.name: MFJ, only primary spouse has a small private IRA withdrawal; spouse still working
scenarios.source: Same Form MO-A Section B mechanics as the second scenario, but only the primary (age 66) has a $4,000 IRA withdrawal; the spouse (age 58, still working) has $20,000 of unrelated wage income and no retirement income of her own. Line3 = 24000-0 = 24000, under the $32,000 MFJ threshold, so Line4(32000) > Line3(24000) and Line5 = $0 (no reduction). Line7 = min(4000,6000) = 4000 (only the primary contributes; the spouse's column is $0). Line9 = 4000-0 = 4000, the full withdrawal is excluded. Missouri AGI = 24000-4000 = 20000. Standard deduction (MFJ, primary 66 qualifies for the $1,650 addback and the $6,000 OBBBA senior bonus at this income; spouse 58 does not) = 32200+1650+6000 = 39850, which alone exceeds the $24,000 of income. Taxable income = $0 either before or after the $4,000 exclusion. Tax = $0.
